desc:
A shop has lanes checkout lanes. Customer i is given as customers[i] = [arrival, service]: they arrive at time arrival and need service time units at a lane. The array is sorted by arrival time and customers are served strictly in this order.

Each customer goes to the lane that becomes free the earliest (a lane that is already idle counts as free). If that lane is still busy, the customer waits until it is free; service starts at max(arrival, time the lane becomes free). A customer's waiting time is the start of service minus the arrival. Return the sum of the waiting times of all customers.

lanes = 2, customers = [[0,5],[1,3],[2,4],[3,2]]
c0: lane A, starts 0 (wait 0), lane A busy until 5
c1: lane B, starts 1 (wait 0), lane B busy until 4
c2: lane B frees first (4), starts 4 (wait 2), busy until 8
c3: lane A frees first (5), starts 5 (wait 2)
answer = 4
constraints: 0 ≤ arrival ≤ 10<sup>6</sup>, arrivals are in non-decreasing order
hints: Simulate the customers one by one in the given order. What do you need to know about the lanes when a customer arrives?
Only the moment each lane becomes free matters, and the customer always takes the lane that becomes free first.

Keep a min-heap with one entry per lane holding its free time (all zeros at the start). For each customer pop the smallest free time f, start at max(arrival, f), add start - arrival to the answer and push start + service.
editorial: The lane identity never matters, only the set of free times. The customer picks the smallest free time, so a min-heap of the free times is exactly the right structure: pop the earliest, compute the start, push the new free time.

Because a lane that is free earlier than the arrival can serve the customer immediately, the start time is max(arrival, f) and the waiting time is never negative. Each customer costs two heap operations on a heap of size lanes, so the total is O(n log lanes) time and O(lanes) space.
The total can reach about 1.25 × 10<sup>9</sup> (5,000 customers of length 100 on one lane, all arriving at time 0), which is why the limits are chosen so that the sum still fits in a 32-bit integer.
solution:
import heapq


def totalWait(lanes, customers):
    free = [0] * lanes
    total = 0
    for arrival, service in customers:
        f = heapq.heappop(free)
        start = max(arrival, f)
        total += start - arrival
        heapq.heappush(free, start + service)
    return total
